mission: mteb upstream contribution recon for KazQAD tasks PR (2026-07-04)

findings.claim: Adding a task/dataset to mteb requires 4 steps: implement a task subclass, fill out TaskMetadata, calculate descriptive statistics, submit a PR.
findings.quote:
To add a new task or dataset to MTEB, you need to do four things:

1. **Implement a new task**: Implement a task with the desired dataset, by subclassing an abstract task
2. **Fill out the metadata** describing the task, main scores, languages etc.
3. **Calculate descriptive statistics**, which is used to detect duplicates, few number of samples or very short documents
4. **Submit a Pull Request** of the edits to the [MTEB](https://github.com/embeddings-benchmark/mteb/blob/main) repository

findings.claim: CI runs a dedicated dataset-loading workflow keyed off changes to mteb/tasks/**.py, executed via `make dataset-load-test-pr` (or `make dataset-load-test` on push to main), which resolves to a pytest run restricted to the `test_datasets` marker; the base `make test` used for general PR CI explicitly EXCLUDES that marker.
findings.quote:
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "mteb/tasks/**.py" ... run: |
        if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "pull_request" ]; then
          make dataset-load-test-pr BASE_BRANCH=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
        else
          make dataset-load-test
        fi

[Makefile] test:
	uv run --no-sync --group test pytest -n auto -m "not (test_datasets or leaderboard_stability or test_reference_models)"

dataset-load-test:
	uv run --no-sync --group test pytest -m test_datasets

dataset-load-test-pr:
	eval "$$(uv run --no-sync python -m scripts.extract_datasets $(BASE_BRANCH))" && uv run --no-sync --group test pytest -m test_datasets

findings.claim: Commit message convention (not strictly enforced but recommended): prefix `dataset:` for new datasets/benchmarks to trigger semantic-release version bump; `fix:` patch, `feat:` minor, `breaking:` major, `model:` for new models; `docs:`/`chore:`/`refactor:` do not bump version and following this isn't required if you don't intend to trigger a release.
findings.quote: For maintainers (and contributors), this means that commits with the following prefixes will automatically trigger a version bump: - `fix:` for patches - `model:` for new models - `dataset:` for new datasets and benchmarks - `feat:` for minor versions - `breaking:` for major versions ... Other prefixes will not trigger a version bump ... you're not required to follow this convention when contributing to MTEB.

findings.claim: Uploading the dataset to a specific HF org is NOT strictly mandated to open the PR — `dataset.path` can point to any existing HF dataset repo (e.g. third-party org) — but a `push_dataset_to_hub(repo_name)` helper exists and the convention shown in docs uses the `mteb/` org (e.g. `mteb/poem_sentiment`, `mteb/CQADupstackAndroidRetrieval`) after processing, which is recommended so dataset_transform preprocessing doesn't have to be re-run.
findings.quote:
Once a dataset is added to the repository, it can be pushed to the hub using the [`push_dataset_to_hub`][mteb.AbsTask.push_dataset_to_hub] method. ... You can then update class to utilize the new dataset on the hub and remove the `dataset_transform` method. ... task = MyTask()
repo_name = f"myorg/{task.metadata.name}"
task.push_dataset_to_hub(repo_name)

findings.claim: There is no separate, non-deprecated `AbsTaskReranking` base class anymore. All modern reranking tasks (and all modern retrieval tasks) subclass `AbsTaskRetrieval` directly; `type="Reranking"` in TaskMetadata is what distinguishes them, not the Python base class.

The old `AbsTaskReranking` class still exists at mteb/abstasks/text/reranking.py, but is decorated `@deprecated` and only kept for one legacy dataset-format code path (`transform_old_dataset_format` for tasks listed in `OLD_FORMAT_RERANKING_TASKS`, currently an empty list). New PRs should not use it.

`AbsTaskRetrieval` (mteb/abstasks/retrieval.py) is a subclass of the generic `AbsTask` and defines class attributes ignore_identical_ids, abstask_prompt, k_values=(1,3,5,10,20,100,1000), skip_first_result, plus load_data(), evaluate(), convert_to_reranking(), push_dataset_to_hub()-adjacent helpers, and a v1->v2 dataset-format converter (convert_v1_dataset_format_to_v2) for backward compat with tasks still using the old self.queries/self.corpus/self.relevant_docs attributes.
findings.quote:
class AbsTaskRetrieval(AbsTask):
    ignore_identical_ids: bool = False
    abstask_prompt = "Retrieve text based on user query."
    k_values: Sequence[int] = (1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 100, 1000)
    _top_k: int = max(k_values)
    dataset: dict[str, dict[str, RetrievalSplitData]]
    _support_cross_encoder: bool = True
    _support_search: bool = True
    _previous_results_model_meta: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    skip_first_result: bool = False

findings.claim: `AbsTaskRetrieval.load_data()` reads `self.metadata.dataset['path']`, `['revision']`, and optional `.get('trust_remote_code', False)`, then for each eval split (and each hf_subset if multilingual) instantiates `RetrievalDatasetLoader(hf_repo=..., revision=..., trust_remote_code=..., split=..., config=hf_subset).load(num_proc=...)`, storing results in `self.dataset[hf_subset][split]` as a `RetrievalSplitData`. Finally it calls `self.dataset_transform()` and sets `self.data_loaded = True`.

`RetrievalDatasetLoader` expects the HF dataset repo to expose specific HF 'config' names it auto-discovers via get_dataset_config_names: `{subset}-corpus` (or plain `corpus` for non-multilingual), `{subset}-queries` (or `queries`), a qrels config (`qrels` if not subset-specific), and OPTIONALLY `{subset}-top_ranked` (or plain `top_ranked`) which, if present, is loaded and used to populate the RetrievalSplitData's `top_ranked` field for reranking-style evaluation.

findings.claim: `TaskMetadata` is a Pydantic `BaseModel` with `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` (unknown kwargs raise). The genuinely REQUIRED fields (no default value) are: `dataset` (MetadataDatasetDict), `name`, `description`, `type` (TaskType literal), `eval_langs` (Languages), `main_score`. All other fields have defaults: `prompt=None`, `modalities=["text"]`, `category=None`, `reference=None`, `eval_splits=["test"]`, `date=None`, `domains=None`, `task_subtypes=None`, `license=None`, `annotations_creators=None`, `dialect=None`, `sample_creation=None`, `bibtex_citation=None`, `adapted_from=None`, `is_public=True`, `contributed_by=None`, `superseded_by=None`, `is_beta=False`.

findings.claim: There is NO `descriptive_stats` (or `n_samples`) field passed into `TaskMetadata(...)` at all in current mteb — this is a change from older mteb versions. Instead `descriptive_stats` and `n_samples` are read-only `@property`s that lazily load a separate auto-generated JSON file at `mteb/descriptive_stats/{TaskType}/{TaskName}.json` (or under an `Image/` subfolder for MIEB task types). The JSON is produced by calling `task.calculate_descriptive_statistics()` on an instantiated, loaded task, which writes stats per split (num_samples, character-length stats for docs/queries, relevant_docs_statistics, top_ranked_statistics, num_documents, num_queries).

Contributor docs confirm the descriptive-stats workflow above and give the exact PR checklist: implement task -> fill metadata -> `task.calculate_descriptive_statistics()` -> import the class in the directory's `__init__.py` -> submit PR. It explicitly says all TaskMetadata fields must be filled for a task to be merged (fields may be None only in draft PRs, to be resolved during review).
findings.quote: 1. **Implement a new task** ... 2. **Fill out the metadata** ... 3. **Calculate descriptive statistics**, which is used to detect duplicates, few number of samples or very short documents 4. **Submit a Pull Request** ... To run a task locally you do not necessarily need to fill out all the fields in the `TaskMetadata`, but if you want to include the dataset in `mteb` we require that all fields are filled out. ... place task inside the `mteb/tasks` directory, and make sure to import the task in the `__init__.py` file in the same directory. ... To calculate the descriptive statistics, you can run `task.calculate_descriptive_statistics()`.

findings.claim: Retrieval tasks live at mteb/tasks/retrieval/<iso639-3-lang-or-'multilingual'>/*.py (e.g. eng/, rus/, ara/, code/, dan/, deu/...), and reranking tasks live in the sibling tree mteb/tasks/reranking/<lang>/*.py, but reranking task Python classes still subclass AbsTaskRetrieval (see finding above) — the directory split (retrieval/ vs reranking/) is purely organizational, not a base-class split. There is currently NO Kazakh (kaz) directory or task file anywhere under mteb/tasks/ (retrieval, reranking, or otherwise) — a Kazakh contribution would be a net-new `mteb/tasks/retrieval/kaz/` (and optionally `mteb/tasks/reranking/kaz/`) directory.

findings.claim: The `TaskType` literal (required field `type=`) includes both `"Retrieval"` and `"Reranking"` as first-class values among a much larger unified list spanning text/image/audio/video task types (MIEB/MAEB/MVEB additions merged in the v2.0.0 breaking release).

A retrieval task can be converted, at runtime, into a reranking-style evaluation from a previous model's saved predictions via `AbsTaskRetrieval.convert_to_reranking(top_ranked_path, top_k=10)`, which loads a JSON of a prior run's per-query scored candidates and truncates to top_k per query — an alternative to pre-baking a static top_ranked column into the HF dataset.

findings.claim: mteb has a formal, enforced concept of 'private' tasks (is_public=False) distinct from a gated HF repo: an explicit allowlist test fails the CI suite for any is_public=False task whose name is not on a maintainer-curated list, forcing every private/restricted dataset PR to get an explicit maintainer sign-off baked into the test file itself.

mteb's own hub-integration code explicitly imports and handles huggingface_hub's GatedRepoError as an expected condition when checking commits/files on the Hub (logs a warning and returns None rather than crashing), i.e. the library is written to tolerate encountering gated repos gracefully, though this is a defensive fallback, not evidence that gated repos pass the CI dataset-loading test.

mteb runs a dedicated CI job, 'Datasets available on HuggingFace' (.github/workflows/dataset_loading.yml), on every PR that touches mteb/tasks/**.py; it actually calls load_data() for changed/added tasks using an HF_TOKEN secret that only maintainers control. A dataset gated on HF would only load in this CI if the account behind the mteb org's HF_TOKEN has itself accepted that dataset's gate terms on huggingface.co beforehand — a PR author cannot make their own gate-acceptance count for CI.

...
    - name: Run dataset loading tests

findings.claim: mteb's official PR checklist (linked from PR bodies, e.g. #4226) requires: explaining the gap the dataset fills, confirming the dataset loads via the mteb package, running at least mteb/baseline-random-encoder plus one small real model (e.g. intfloat/multilingual-e5-small) and pasting scores into the PR, confirming scores are neither trivial/perfect nor random, reducing dataset size if too large, and reproducing paper scores in the PR description if applicable.
findings.quote:
- [ ] I have outlined why this dataset is filling an existing gap in `mteb`
- [ ] I have tested that the dataset runs with the `mteb` package.
- [ ] I have run the following models on the task (adding the results to the pr)...
  - [ ] `mteb/baseline-random encoder`
  - [ ] `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small` or another small model
- [ ] I have checked that the performance is neither trivial (close to perfect scores) nor random.
- [ ] I have considered the size of the dataset and reduced it if it is too big
- [ ] I reproduced scores from the original paper (if applicable)

findings.claim: mteb's semver/commit-message convention treats new dataset PRs as version-bump-triggering: a commit/PR title prefixed 'dataset:' (matching all 5 PR titles examined: 4710, 4487, 4521, 3991, 4226, 3876) auto-triggers a package version bump and PyPI/GitHub release on merge to main, so a Kazakh-retrieval PR should follow the same 'dataset: ...' title convention.
findings.quote:
- `fix:` for patches
- `model:` for new models
- `dataset:` for new datasets and benchmarks
- `feat:` for minor versions
- `breaking:` for major versions

Any commit with one of these prefixes will trigger a version bump upon merging to the main branch

Whether to file the task under 'private' (is_public=False, needs an ACCEPTED_PRIVATE_TASKS allowlist entry reviewed by a maintainer) or push for full public un-gating before the PR — the two precedents that started gated/restricted (BrowseComp-Plus, Elastic KB) both ended up either fully public or is_public=False+mteb-private, never left simply 'gated under the original org', so the PR author should decide which target state to aim for up front and say so explicitly in the PR description to avoid the ~33-day BrowseComp-Plus-style back-and-forth.

Best current reviewer/maintainer to tag for a Kazakh retrieval/reranking dataset PR — Samoed and KennethEnevoldsen appear as reviewers/approvers on all 6 sampled PRs and are the de facto gatekeepers, but no evidence was gathered on who specifically handles non-English/lower-resource language additions or whether there's a language-specific champion (e.g. someone who handled Vietnamese/Danish additions) worth pinging.
